description: Robustness of the memory router against untrusted / malformed LLM output: reasoning-leak, CJK-leak, empty/invalid entries, malformed JSON, and null/non-array shapes. Links to 12 §4 (recalled memory is untrusted). Prompt-injection round-trip-inert, delimiter-collision escaping and recall caps (14 §6) are v2-spec requirements absent in v1 and registered as GAP-05. T14-08 closed the formatter-level slice (`adversarial.recall.*`: additionalContext sanitization/escaping/caps, spec 11 §5/12 §4) with real unit tests in `crates/memory/src/recall/format.rs`. T16-04 closes GAP-05's remaining end-to-end slice (stored memory -> real op engine -> wired recall -> inert output, `adversarial.recall.end-to-end-*`) plus the adjacent corpus the card also names -- malicious indexed code (`adversarial.code.*`), source secrets and symlink escapes through the real scan/reconcile/build pipeline (`adversarial.index.*`), and hook-captured secrets never touching disk (`adversarial.hook.*`) -- each case's `provenance.ref` names the real Rust test that asserts it. This family has no generic JSON-loading runner (unlike `parser`/`fault`); every case here, T14-08's and T16-04's alike, is a hand-written test that documents its fixture-id correspondence in `provenance`/comments rather than loading this file at runtime. D-097 adds `adversarial.redaction.*`: a labelled precision/recall corpus for the shared secret scanner (spec 12 §2), derived from a live measurement in which 32 of 43 files skipped `reason='secret'` in one real repository were false positives, each costing the whole file (spec 12 §5). Both halves are gated together by `crates/core/tests/redaction_corpus.rs`, which loads this file at runtime -- unlike the hand-written cases above it. Case texts are minimal reconstructions of the measured mechanisms, never copies of the source they were measured on.

cases.title: A credential in a URL query string is a secret

provenance.source: D-099, found by D-097's true-positive corpus
provenance.note: is_token_byte counts = + / as token bytes, so `?k=ghp_...` is ONE token whose prefix check fails; the most ordinary shape of a leaked token was undetected in rule set v1 as much as in v2

cases.title: A plain environment-variable assignment is not a secret

provenance.source: D-100, found by D-098's live acceptance
provenance.note: is_token_byte accepts = - _, so this is ONE 48-character token with a digit, lowercase and uppercase: it clears the length bar, D-097's mixed-class rule and the entropy threshold alike. It cost cronjob/redis-backup/docs/monitoring-and-restore.md its whole file

cases.title: A real secret assigned to an environment variable is still a secret

provenance.source: D-100, found by D-098's live acceptance

cases.title: Base64 whose only = is trailing padding is a secret

provenance.source: D-100, found by D-098's live acceptance
provenance.note: why splitting on = is safe: in base64, = occurs only as padding at the tail, so the part before it is the whole key. A real secret, measured in pm2.ecosystem.yml

cases.title: A token long enough only because of its name is not a secret

provenance.source: D-100 mutation testing
provenance.note: the whole token is 47 characters but its value part is 32 -- below ENTROPY_MIN_LEN, which is the bar for a plausible key. Measuring the length on the token while judging the shape on the part survived mutation until this case existed
